title: In a flat-level model near 1981, Locarno group counts fell 5.9% relative to Kislovodsk
abstract: We compare Locarno groups and weighted Wolf counts with Kislovodsk groups on 1,353 common dates in November 1978 to June 1983. At matched F10.7 in a flat-level model, the group ratio falls by 5.89% (conditional 95% limits -9.60% to -2.07%). Both archives show fewer groups at matched emission. Cortesi-only dates give a smaller, uncertain ratio change of -3.50%. Separate local time slopes include no change in the group ratio. Weighted Wolf counts per Kislovodsk group change by -4.81% with flat levels and -19.04% with separate slopes. An exact fitted decomposition connects these results. The main model opposes a 14% group loss confined to Locarno. The evidence does not identify a solar cause, a counting fault, or smaller spots. Prior work already compared the long station records. This study adds a direct same-date test of the specified emission anomaly and its model limits. Code, aggregate estimates, a figure and exact source hashes are included. External observations stay outside the publication.

display.caption: Paired archive changes near January 1981 under flat levels and separate local time slopes. Intervals are conditional 95% limits from six-month residual blocks.
